task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
separability of role coverage from talent and possession counts
talent control in lineup-level influence models
methodological_questions: Can lineup role coverage be separated from player talent and usage/count measures?
Does talent control hold when role coverage varies within team-seasons?
What exposure, sample size, and label-derivation risks affect lineup-level role coverage tests?
evidence_establishes: No earlier study from this project was returned by retrieve_history for this question, so no prior finding on lineup role coverage, within-team variation, or talent control is established by the retrieved record.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether lineup role coverage varies within teams in this data.
Whether role coverage is separable from talent or counts.
Whether any talent control works as intended.
The reliability of role labels, lineup exposure, or any effect size.
own_inferences: Role labels (organizer, shaper, terminal) appear to be built from [source]-derived possession records (initiator, play type, points). If points or the possession outcome enter the label, role coverage is partly a function of the outcome it is meant to explain.
Coverage of a role within a lineup is close to a count-like quantity that scales with minutes and possessions, so separating it from counts needs an explicit model rather than a descriptive check.
With 90 team-seasons, within-team variation is the main information source. Lineup-level exposure is likely sparse for many lineup-role combinations.
No talent metric is named in the data description beyond box-score and matchup-derived proxies, so talent control may be incomplete or itself error-prone.
uncertainties: The exact operational definitions of organizer, shaper and terminal are not given in the task, so their dependence on points or outcomes cannot be checked.
Lineup minute and possession distributions are not reported.
The talent measure to be used for control is not specified.

Whether 2025-26 data (regular season complete from 2026-04-13; playoffs complete from 2026-06-21) should be pooled with 2022-23 to 2024-25 is unresolved. The stated unit count of 90 team-seasons appears to cover the three complete seasons only.
Retrieval returned zero records, so there is no evidence on whether this question was studied before.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned no records. The decision rests on the task statement and data description alone. It is not shaped by earlier results, failed approaches, or prior work.

blocking_constraints.text: Role labels derived from play-type records with points may encode the outcome being explained. Coverage can then be partly a restatement of scoring.
Lineup-role combinations are likely to have few possessions for many lineups, so within-lineup estimates are unstable without minimum-exposure rules.
Role coverage is correlated with talent, usage, and lineup composition. Separating it from talent requires a talent measure that is not clearly specified or measured without error.
Talent proxies from box-score and matchup data may be noisy, so residual talent confounding may remain after control.

prior_work.summary: No prior work was retrieved, so no identifier is cited. Whether earlier work answered this question cannot be determined from the retrieval result.

risks.text: If organizer, shaper or terminal labels use points or possession outcome, the coverage variable is partly built from the response. Role definitions must be fixed without outcome information.
Talent, usage and lineup quality are plausibly related to role coverage, so the talent control may leave a confounded association in place.
Talent and role measures from play-by-play and box-score proxies may have low reliability, which attenuates controls and biases coefficients.
Between 90 team-seasons, the within-team contrasts needed to separate coverage from talent may be too small for useful power.
Many lineup-role cells will have very few possessions, so estimates for rare cells will be unstable and dominated by noise.
Three roles, several coverage definitions and multiple lineup thresholds create many comparisons unless one primary specification is fixed in advance.
Without placebo roles or shuffled role assignments, an apparent coverage effect may just reflect possession counts or minutes.
Using full-season or full-playoff role totals to predict within-season outcomes leaks future information. Partial 2025-26 playoff data before 2026-06-21 must be excluded.
Play-type frequencies and scoring environment change across the 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons. Pooling without season effects can produce spurious coverage differences.
Joining play-by-play, substitution intervals and [source]-derived possession records may misalign lineups and possessions. Reconciliation checks are needed before analysis.

design.estimand: Within team-season association between lineup role coverage (at least one organizer, shaper, or terminal on court) and lineup-level possession outcome (points per possession), conditional on a pre-specified talent proxy and possession count, with coverage shown to be separable from talent and count.
design.unit: Lineup-season possession record, with possessions nested in lineups, lineups nested in team-seasons.
design.sample: Regular-season and playoff possessions from 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 (the 90 team-seasons). Lineups need a pre-set minimum possession count. The 2025-26 regular season may be added only as a held-out check once complete (from 2026-04-13). The 2025-26 playoffs may be used only after completion (from 2026-06-21). No partial files.
design.power: Before analysis, run a simulation using the observed possession distribution to find the minimum detectable coverage effect at 80% power. State that effect. If it is unattainable at the lineup-count threshold, report the test as underpowered.
design.controls: Role definitions fixed before analysis and built without points or possession outcome. Talent control from pre-specified box-score and matchup proxies, with a reliability check. Possession count, minutes, lineup size, season and team fixed effects. Coverage tested for correlation with talent and count (separability check) before the main model.
design.falsification: Placebo roles (labels shuffled within team-season) and a placebo outcome (points from non-role possessions) must show no coverage effect. Coverage effect should disappear after conditioning on talent proxies if it is confounded. A failed placebo or a non-separable coverage variable stops the claim.
design.multiplicity: One primary specification (coverage at or above one role, minimum exposure threshold, team-season random intercepts). Other coverage definitions and thresholds are secondary and reported with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Claim support only if the primary coefficient is positive with a pre-specified interval excluding zero, survives talent control, the separability check passes, and placebo roles show no effect. Otherwise report as inconclusive or artifact.
design.data_version: Frozen snapshot of NBA stats API files for 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular and playoffs, plus 2025-26 regular season after 2026-04-13 and 2025-26 playoffs after 2026-06-21, with versioned graph-derived possession records and a record of the question date (2026-07-13).
